content:
Requirement R07 (input): Report Surveillance Event. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to report a surveillance event as it happens..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-07.1, F-07.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: 2-3 distinct interaction flows, labeled Be-07.<F>.1, Be-07.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-07.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent:** Enable the pilot to report a surveillance event to C2 the moment it is observed, in flight.

Function candidates:

**F-07.1 — Pilot commits an observed surveillance event to C2.**
The teleology: the artefact exists to get a detected event out of the cockpit and into the C2 report channel. Measurable effect: an event report is transmitted and acknowledged.

**F-07.2 — Pilot classifies/qualifies the reported event.**
Distinct goal: not just "an event happened" but *what kind* — attaching event type/attributes to the report. Opens a categorization interaction rather than a commit interaction.

**F-07.3 — Pilot geo-anchors the event to its observed location.**
Distinct goal: tie the report to a POI/AOI on the map so C2 receives *where* it occurred, not just that it occurred.

---

Note on distinctness vs R05: R05 (F-05.1) already covers *submit structured intel reports to C2* via the map-anchored press-and-hold pattern. F-07.3 here risks collapsing into R05's goal — geo-anchoring + commit is essentially the same interaction pattern already closed. I'd flag **F-07.3 as a likely reuse of R05's Behaviour/Structure**, not a genuinely new Function.

That leaves F-07.1 (commit) and F-07.2 (classify) as the genuinely distinct pair. The tension in this requirement is *speed* — "as it happens" implies a low-friction one-action commit (F-07.1) may conflict with the richer classification of F-07.2.

My recommendation: close on **F-07.1** as the primary Function, treating classification as a possible sub-behaviour rather than a separate Function unless you want event-typing to be a first-class goal.

Which way do you want to go?
I believe the correct one should be .2

Reasonable — if the report's *value* to C2 is the event type/attributes, then classification is the real goal, not the bare commit.

But note the framing shift this forces: **F-07.2 as stated presupposes an event is already being reported** ("classifies/qualifies *the reported* event"). If we make it the primary Function, it has to stand on its own — the commit becomes subordinate. Let me restate it cleanly so it's a self-contained teleology:

**F-07.2 (restated) — Pilot reports a surveillance event *with its classification* to C2.**
The artefact exists so that C2 receives a *typed/qualified* event report as it happens. Measurable effect: a classified event report is transmitted and acknowledged. The commit is the delivery mechanism; the classification is what gives the report its operational meaning.

This absorbs F-07.1's transmit outcome into F-07.2 rather than leaving two competing Functions — otherwise you'd have "commit" and "classify" both claiming the same report, which isn't cleanly distinct.

One caution against the "as it happens" intent: classification adds interaction steps (picking a type). We'll need the Behaviour to keep that fast under high workload — but that's a Behaviour-layer concern, correctly deferred.

Confirming the Function label as:

**F-07.2 — Pilot reports a surveillance event with its classification to C2.**

Good to close the Function layer here?

**Function layer closed: F-07.2 — Pilot reports a surveillance event with its classification to C2.**

---

Behaviour candidates (Touch / Keyboard, modality-complete):

**Be-07.2.1 — Classify-then-commit (map-anchored, R05 pattern extended).**
Press-and-hold on Map at the observed location → option ring appears → select event-type marker from ring → report auto-populates with type + location → commit/send. Keyboard path: bezel OSS to open report, UCP/rotary to step through event types, OSS to commit.
- Pro: directly reuses R05's proven map-anchored structure; location comes "for free."
- Con: press-and-hold + ring traversal is several actions — slowest against "as it happens."

**Be-07.2.2 — Preset event-type quick-commit.**
A small set of pre-defined event-type buttons (e.g. the mission's expected event categories) always visible during a surveillance task. One tap on the type = classify + commit in a single action; location auto-tagged from current UAV sensor/aircraft position. Keyboard path: each type mapped to a dedicated bezel OSS, one press = send.
- Pro: fastest — single action satisfies "as it happens" best.
- Con: only works for a bounded, pre-agreed event vocabulary; no free qualification.

**Be-07.2.3 — Two-stage: quick-flag then enrich.**
Single action drops a time-stamped event flag immediately (captures the moment), then an editable report card opens allowing the pilot to set/refine the classification and send when ready. Keyboard path: OSS to flag, UCP to classify, OSS to send.
- Pro: reconciles the speed/richness tension — the *moment* is captured instantly, classification isn't rushed.
- Con: two-phase flow; the report isn't complete until the enrich step, so an interrupted task could leave an unclassified flag.

---

Recommendation: **Be-07.2.3**. It's the only candidate that honors both halves of F-07.2 — "as it happens" (instant flag) *and* "with its classification" (deliberate enrich) — without forcing a bounded vocabulary like Be-07.2.2 or paying the full ring-traversal cost of Be-07.2.1 at the critical moment.

Note: Be-07.2.1 shares R05's map/ring/preset/marker structure — if you pick it, it's largely reuse, not new build.

Which flow?
What were the behaviours on the R05?

From the prior requirements record, R05 closed on a single Behaviour:

**Be-05.1 — press-and-hold on Map → option ring → select preset marker → commit/send**, modality-complete (Touch/Keyboard).

Structure was: Map view + option ring + preset buttons + marker glyph layer — all logged as reused/shared with R06/R07 (the "map-anchored task pattern").

Only that one Behaviour was carried forward; the record doesn't list rejected Be alternatives for R05, just the closed one. Also logged there: a spin-off for *voice-annotated reporting* as a separate undesigned Function.

So my Be-07.2.1 above is deliberately the R05 pattern re-applied — that's why I flagged it as reuse rather than new build.

**Behaviour layer closed: Be-07.2.1 — classify-then-commit, map-anchored (R05 pattern extended).**
Press-and-hold on Map at observed location → option ring → select event-type marker → report auto-populates (type + location) → commit/send. Modality-complete: Touch (WAD) and Keyboard (bezel OSS + UCP/rotary) paths both complete the full task.

Since this is explicitly the R05 pattern, most structure is reuse. The only genuinely *new* piece is the event-type content in the ring (surveillance event categories vs. R05's intel preset markers).

---

Structure candidates:

**S-07.2.1.1 — Full reuse of R05 map-anchored structure, event-type ring variant.**
- Map view (reused, shared R05/R06)
- Option ring (reused) — populated with **surveillance event-type entries** instead of intel presets
- Preset buttons → surveillance event-type presets (new content, same widget)
- Marker glyph layer (reused) — event marker glyphs added
- Keyboard: bezel OSS to open/commit, UCP/rotary to step event types (reused mapping)
- Pro: minimal new build; consistent pilot interaction across R05/R06/R07. Con: ring shared across report types risks category clutter if intel + surveillance vocabularies coexist.

**S-07.2.1.2 — Reuse map/ring/marker, add a dedicated Surveillance Event overlay layer.**
- Same reused base (Map, ring, marker layer)
- **New stacked overlay layer** scoped to the active surveillance task — ring shows only that task's event types; overlay auto-arms when a surveillance order is active (from R06 order channel)
- Keyboard path identical to S-07.2.1.1
- Pro: keeps surveillance event vocabulary isolated from intel presets (avoids clutter); context-scoped ring is faster. Con: one new overlay layer to build + arming logic tied to R06 order state.

**S-07.2.1.3 — Reuse structure, surveillance types entered via UCP free-code rather than ring presets.**
- Map + marker layer reused; ring reduced to a single "surveillance event" entry
- Classification via **UCP alphanumeric entry** (event code/type typed)
- Pro: unbounded classification vocabulary. Con: typing under high workload contradicts "as it happens"; weakest Touch path (UCP-centric) strains modality-completeness.

---

Recommendation: **S-07.2.1.2**. It reuses the R05 base but scopes the event ring to the active surveillance task, which keeps the vocabulary clean and the selection fast — matching F-07.2's "as it happens" better than the shared-ring S-07.2.1.1, and without S-07.2.1.3's typing penalty. The only cost is a context-armed overlay tied to the R06 order state, which is a natural link (surveillance report answers a surveillance order).

Flag: the Map, marker glyph layer, and ring widget remain **shared assets across R05/R06/R07** — S-07.2.1.2 adds a surveillance-scoped layer on top, not a duplicate.

Which structure?
What were the strcutures of the R05?

From the prior requirements record, R05's structure (under Be-05.1) was:

- **Map view** (already-implemented screen, reused)
- **Option ring** (new widget at R05)
- **Preset buttons** (preset marker selection)
- **Marker glyph layer** (overlay on the map)

All four logged as **reused/shared with R06/R07** — the "map-anchored task pattern."

Also noted at R05: a Touchpad hardware proposal was **rejected** (not in baseline), so classification/pointing stays on WAD Touch + TDC + bezel/UCP.

So my S-07.2.1.1 is that exact set with surveillance event-type content; S-07.2.1.2 adds one surveillance-scoped overlay layer on top of it.

So...
- S-07.1.1 — Map view (WAD), reused.
- S-07.1.2 — Option ring (radial menu overlay at selected point.
- S-07.1.3 — Preset marker buttons (intel taxonomy).
- S-07.1.4 — Marker glyph layer (committed markers on map).
- S-07.1.5 — Input bindings: Touch (hold+tap) / Keyboard (bezel rotary+OSS).

You're relabeling the R05 structure elements as a decomposed list and reusing them for R07. Two issues to flag before we lock it:

**1. Label indexing.** Your labels read `S-07.1.x`, but our closed indices for this requirement are **F-07.2** and **Be-07.2.1**. So the correct prefix is `S-07.2.1.x`, not `S-07.1.x`. (The "1" in R05's world was F-05.1/Be-05.1 — different requirement.)

**2. These are shared assets, not new R07 structures.** Items 1–4 are the *same physical/software elements* already defined at R05, not R07-specific copies. Per the cardinality rule, they should be referenced as shared, not duplicated. Only the **content** changes for R07: the ring/preset taxonomy is *surveillance event types*, not intel markers.

So the corrected, consistent set:

- **S-07.2.1.1** — Map view (WAD) — *shared, reused from R05/R06.*
- **S-07.2.1.2** — Option ring (radial overlay at selected point) — *shared widget, reused from R05.*
- **S-07.2.1.3** — Preset marker buttons — *shared widget; **surveillance event taxonomy** as R07-specific content.*
- **S-07.2.1.4** — Marker glyph layer (committed event markers on map) — *shared layer, reused.*
- **S-07.2.1.5** — Input bindings: Touch (hold+tap) / Keyboard (bezel rotary + OSS) — *shared binding pattern, reused.*

This is effectively my **S-07.2.1.1** proposal (full reuse, event-type variant) — you've dropped the context-scoped overlay from my S-07.2.1.2. That's a defensible call: simpler, one fewer new element, at the cost of intel + surveillance vocabularies sharing one ring.

Want to confirm this set (full-reuse, surveillance taxonomy as content), or add the surveillance-scoped overlay?

**Structure layer closed.** Full-reuse of the R05 map-anchored pattern, surveillance event taxonomy as R07-specific content:

- **S-07.2.1.1** — Map view (WAD) — shared, reused R05/R06.
- **S-07.2.1.2** — Option ring (radial overlay at selected point) — shared widget, reused R05.
- **S-07.2.1.3** — Preset marker buttons — shared widget; **surveillance event taxonomy** as R07-specific content.
- **S-07.2.1.4** — Marker glyph layer (committed event markers) — shared layer, reused R05.
- **S-07.2.1.5** — Input bindings: Touch (hold+tap) / Keyboard (bezel rotary + OSS) — shared binding pattern, both modality-complete.

---

**R07 closed:**
- **F-07.2** — Pilot reports a surveillance event with its classification to C2.
- **Be-07.2.1** — Classify-then-commit, map-anchored (R05 pattern): press-and-hold on Map → option ring → select event-type marker → auto-populate (type + location) → commit/send. Modality-complete (Touch / Keyboard).
- **Structure S-07.2.1.1–.5** as above — entirely shared with R05/R06 except the surveillance event taxonomy content.

Consistency note for later consolidation: R07 adds no new hardware and no new widgets — only new taxonomy content on the shared ring/preset. The intel-vs-surveillance vocabulary coexistence on one ring is the open item flagged (not resolved here; would surface if ring clutter becomes a concern across R05/R06/R07).

Ready for R08 when you are.
